answer.origin: Primary source: NVIDIA Corporation's own Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR), dated and reporting August 17, 2026, with Items 1.01, 2.03 and 7.01. Stated event time August 17, 2026; the filing is the company's direct disclosure, not a secondary report.
answer.note: Material source claim: on August 17, 2026 NVIDIA entered multiple residual value guaranties with SB Energy (Lessor) covering leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at the Portsmouth Site (PORTS Technology Campus, Pike County, Ohio), with an affiliate of OpenAI Group PBC as tenant. The filing says NVIDIA can provide credit support for an additional ~3.8 GW at its sole discretion, and that NVIDIA's aggregate payment obligation is capped at $105 billion for the initial commitment. What it supports: NVIDIA has taken on a signed, multi-year contingent guarantee obligation, not merely a plan. Payment is triggered by an OpenAI affiliate insolvency-driven default or payment failure, and the shortfall between a guaranteed minimum lease value and replacement-lease or sale recoveries is payable. Payment conditions include the Lessor satisfying ready-for-service conditions, expected beginning in 2028. Each Agreement generally becomes effective on lease commencement and terminates at the earliest of the 20th anniversary of commencement, OpenAI lease termination, OpenAI obtaining a satisfactory credit rating, or other customary events. OpenAI has agreed to reimburse and indemnify NVIDIA for amounts actually paid. Conditional interpretation: the $105 billion cap and the 4.25 GW initial commitment are the company's disclosed exposure, the realistic cash exposure depends on OpenAI's ability to pay and on recoveries from re-leasing or sale, and the additional 3.8 GW is optional and undisclosed as to amount. The claim is a company filing, so it supports the existence and terms of the commitment as stated; it does not establish future payments. Forward-looking statements are flagged in the filing.
limitations: The full text of the Agreements is not in the record; the filing says the form will be filed as an exhibit to the Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended July 26, 2026, so the minimum guaranteed lease values, shortfall formula and recovery mechanics are only described qualitatively.
The guaranteed minimum value amounts and lease economics are not disclosed, so the size of the expected shortfall cannot be estimated from this source.

Lease commencement dates and their timing across the 4.25 GW are not disclosed beyond ready-for-service conditions expected beginning in 2028, so when the guarantees become effective is not established.
The $105 billion cap applies to the initial commitment only; the amount, timing and conditions for the optional ~3.8 GW credit support are not quantified.
Credit standing of OpenAI's affiliate tenant is not assessed in this source, so the likelihood of a Trigger Event is unknown.
The press release (Exhibit 99.1) is referenced but its content is not included in the supplied record beyond the subject matter.
No accounting treatment, reserve or recognized liability is disclosed in the supplied text, so the balance-sheet effect is unknown.
follow_up: Retrieve the Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended July 26, 2026 and check the filed Agreements for the guaranteed minimum value, cap mechanics, lease commencement conditions and termination terms.
Review the Exhibit 99.1 press release for any additional quantities, timing or description of the 3.8 GW optional credit support.
Check NVIDIA's 10-Q and subsequent filings for the accounting treatment of the guarantees, any recognized liability, and any disclosed commitments or contingencies.
Monitor lease commencement announcements or ready-for-service disclosures for the Portsmouth Site to establish when the guarantees become effective.
Check public disclosures or credit assessments of OpenAI and its affiliates to evaluate the Trigger Event risk and the reimbursement counterparty's capacity.
